leaves.label: Clear selected deletion records
leaves.path: Media files, metadata and viewing
notes: Selected old/default thumbnail menu offers exact singular/plural clear-deletion labels only when selected flattened files include physical local-storage deletion records. Real current selection at QAction dispatch captures eligible ordered identities before the exact question. Cancel writes nothing; accepted existing scoped writer commits64-record batches independently, preserves trash/re-added/unselected membership and physical queue, and reaches actual importer known_status. New deletions during confirmation remain outside the plan; later error preserves committed prefix and presents warning. Weak visible current main, active captured binding/page, advanced-child and permanent departure epoch guards reject stale menus/answers. Main now has readable Yes/No controls through the existing captured answer transport. Authored measured physical pointer and leaf-specific Return/Escape regressions preserve captured eligibility, full relevant deletion-table/queue state and processed Escape retirement before a usable successor.

Exactly one selected thumbnail context action. Global all-files service clear(None) is already implemented and receives no duplicate credit. No viewer producer or broader media/context parent completion.

Native captured eligibility follows reference: physical local-storage deletion only; flattening/counting collections; current selected media read at menu dispatch; eligible IDs captured before confirmation. Re-add during confirmation keeps current membership, and newly deleted files outside the captured plan remain untouched.

Existing scoped writer preserves trash/current membership and the durable deferred physical deletion queue. This action never physically deletes files or cancels physical queue records. Clearing actual import-status deletion records permits ordinary reimport.

Each batch of up to64 independently commits; the first failing batch aborts subsequent writes without rolling back prior successful batches. The native owner presents Store errors as warnings; reference asynchronous content transport is made synchronous only in copied fixture proof.

Native retained hidden, retired/rebound or different-page callbacks are refused. Actual current-page departure permanently invalidates a menu/answer even after returning; an owned advanced deletion child blocks dispatch/accept. These native ownership boundaries are additional to ordinary Qt modal input blocking, not invented recapture of file eligibility.

recheck.note: Carried (no tag). Replays selected_deletion_records.json (recorded from the real reference menu, question and writer) through the real thumbnail menu and question for labels, question text, batches, re-add/new-delete during question, store tables and reimport status, plus stale-owner guards. Add a tag. Tests: crates/hydrus-gui/tests/gui/selected_deletion_records.rs:48 actual_menu_and_answer_replay_clear_only_captured_records_and_enable_reimport, :204, :278, :539

leaves.label: Time until mouse cursor autohides on media viewer:
leaves.path: File > Options window > media viewer > mouse behaviour
notes: Exact defaultSome700ms noneable control stages/persists/imports media_viewer_cursor_autohide_time_ms with100..100000ms bounds and do not autohide. The actual native viewer owns a Slint SingleShot timer and weak per-WindowId motion callback in the shared desktop ActivityHandler; focus comes from the existing native application observer. Its strict elapsed>delay policy and100..250ms polling (None1000) match fresh real Qt QCursor/QTimer output. Ordinary motion restores the actual cursor and restarts at100ms; accepted hidden drag pauses until ordinary motion resumes. Inactive windows, interactive hover/volume regions and actual open popup stacks restore the cursor and reset the wait. Synchronous native menu show returns establish a fresh wait after blocking timer delivery. Visibility reaches winit set_cursor_visible and the Slint MouseCursor binding; close stops the actual timer and ignores late input. Apply/Cancel, duplicate/other-ID isolation, dead weak registration, actual context-menu open/cancel lifecycle and reopened persisted control value are covered.

Native canvas and existing Slint hover/volume eligibility apply; backend-specific MPV widget input and cursor anchoring remain separate gaps. Slint1.18 internal popup lifecycle is pinned by the repository dependency; synchronous native popup execution uses actual show start/return callbacks while asynchronous menus use the real popup stack. This leaf does not claim cursor anchoring or other mouse-drag controls.

recheck.note: Real viewer and noneable Options row driven with the recorded events of viewer_cursor_options.json (strict threshold, polling interval, focus, popup/menu, hidden drag); the model replays the recorded trace against CursorWait. Amount clamps to 0–1,048,576 and B/KB/MB/GB/TB remain separated binary units; selecting a unit does not convert the amount. Typed values reach the existing query executor with actual Qt hash outcomes for all operator/unit combinations and equality boundaries. Explicit supplied-value reconstruction preserves raw units in the model; native saved-default units persist/reopen and preserve unrelated default families. Cancel leaves the search unchanged. Hidden child/main or pending main questions refuse edits/acceptance; rebind and accepted exit cancel the owned main child, declined exit stays live, and a refused activation is consumed rather than resurrected later. Main-owned lifetime state retires the editor on actual Main-component destruction or final Bound-owner drop as well as rebind/accepted exit, hides owned notices and clears only its own slot. Nonfinal Bound clones, temporary Main hide and pending/declined exit retain the draft; retired/re-shown callbacks and Return cannot publish or change recents/defaults.

Generic active-predicate list editing remains a separate Partial action (audit-options-search-active-edit), excluded from this leaf. The new populated-existing-size lifetime test is a bounded safety check, not generic editing completion; native reopen uses saved typed defaults, while explicit reconstruction remains model-covered.
Separate global radio-Enter preference is outside this finite editor slice; the recorded true-default Enter path is supported.

Reference TB predicate ToString returns error:cannot render this predicate while its typed value/query remain valid; native renders TB explicitly. Existing free-text parser TB limitation stays documented.
All structural/shared predicate editor aliases and Options/filesize parents remain Partial and uncounted. Other predicate kinds retain their existing widgets, model and query semantics.

Qt destruction recording covers two nonmodal standalone QWidget.window() parent cascades with retained wrappers and unchanged blank predicates. It does not destroy client Main, run nested exec() teardown or establish active nested-warning closure. Native notice closure is a separate safety boundary.

notes: Actual days/hours/minutes duration stages/imports/persists/reopens seconds with300-second edited minimum, retaining untouched raw299. Qt uses a controller-global ImageRendererCache. Native owns one cache per Main binding incarnation, shared by its real preview, still viewer, archive/delete and duplicate filter; standalone duplicate filters own separate policy-bound caches. Final Bound-clone drop, rebind and accepted close permanently retire admission while retained worker/callback handles cannot revive it.

Full still-image cache bytes are pending metadata RGB estimates and loaded RGB/RGBA raster bytes recounted at access. The cache admits one incoming item above its soft bound until maintenance, matching Qt. Pending decoders, accepted per-page 64MiB preview snapshots, current canvas/source/resize buffers, Slint image copies, playback and total process/GPU memory are separate presentation/resource ownership and are not evicted or counted as cache bytes.

Percentage uses strict estimated-size admission and applies only to future misses; existing admitted renderers remain subject to ordinary byte/idle maintenance. Saved policy and ICC changes refresh without resetting current accepted media, zoom, generation/page identity or viewing intervals. Future duplicate copies can only reuse cache-owned full rasters, while the current presentation remains independently retained.

Failed full-image and non-image thumbnail/poster fallback remain uncached; decoder injection keeps the public preview Decoder contract and bypasses the production cache. Existing worker bounds and late-publication generation guards are retained. Imported partial resolution falls back to100x100 exactly; real media metadata/ICC identity displaces stale cached sources.

Actual Reset/RetryFailed/RetryIgnored exports now refresh file-count/example caches without changing velocity or gallery examples. Retried files lose hashes exactly as SetStatus(UNKNOWN) does, in both detached exports and the real Apply transaction; reopening exports those persisted caches.

notes: The actual manage-subscriptions Merge button retains the exact initial warning, name-sorted primary choices, name prompt and no-compatible-group information. Each group's primary/name decision is held without changing any draft rows until every group has answered. Cancelling any primary discards the entire pending merge operation; cancelling a name keeps that primary's original name and continues. Completing the last group commits all query moves to the existing draft together. Every absorbed owner is removed before casefolded name allocation; surviving original names and earlier new names remain reserved, including the primary's old name on a case-only rename. Compatibility uses downloader names even when keys differ, as actual Qt does. Primary identity/settings persist, overlapping query texts retain separate queue IDs, full state, file/gallery seed IDs and metadata, and pending log edits. The existing bulk store transaction moves queues before deleting absorbed subscriptions and commits only on list Apply. Parent Cancel drops pending and completed drafts; closed callbacks cannot affect a newly opened owner or its subsequent draft edits.

Qt's no-eaten warning branch is unreachable for stable groups produced by its unchanged GetMergeable: both methods compare the same downloader name. No artificial source mutation or forced warning claim is made.

Native subscription-manager pause-for-editing, bandwidth-wait display, broader import/export, additional-tag editor and other subscription boundaries remain as separately documented. This leaf does not promote the subscriptions parent or aliases.
Qt's modal dialogs are represented by the existing native inline question panel; this change preserves that presentation boundary.
Existing daemon/store concurrency policy remains unchanged. Merge preserves queue identity and writes only edited states/settings; it does not introduce a manager-wide editing lock.
